description: Wire shapes of the usage API, the generation estimate and the usage data model. Rate card: rate-card-v1.json; allowances: allowances-v1.json. Authority: docs/architecture/ai-generation-platform.md section 10 and docs/product/ai-layer-2026-10.md section 5. Conventions (private/no-store, quoted decimal versions, RFC 9457 Problem Details) are those of contracts/decks and contracts/items.

conventions.credits: Integers. A fractional weight or cost is rounded up when it is turned into a debit; the ledger keeps costMicros for exact cost.
conventions.timestamps: UTC, RFC 3339 with seconds. Every day, week and month boundary is a calendar boundary in learning.usage.calendar-zone (Europe/Moscow, owner decision 2026-10-02), expressed here as UTC instants.
conventions.percent: Integer 0..100, rounded half up; percentUsed = (used + reserved) / total, holds included (for FREE too: total is the 50 bar).
conventions.warn: A fair-use bucket sets warn=true above 80% of its monthly limit; the client then shows the quiet counter with its explanation.
conventions.stt: Metered in seconds (usedSeconds); `used` is whole minutes rounded up. MAX has limit null (unlimited within fair use) and velocityPerDay.

ownership.estimateGeneration: AI-01 (#281) owns the endpoint, the rate-card math and the reservation. Spec interpretation (which operations and counts a spec implies) and the personal-data scan hooks are supplied by the generation module as they land (AI-04 and later).

endpoints.note: Read-only: it reserves and persists nothing.

usageResponseFields.period: Current allowance period (a calendar month in the calendar zone) with its periodId; reservations and debits belong to a period.
usageResponseFields.entitlement: The snapshot the numbers came from: source CONFIG (the fallback configured plan), PROMO (a promo code, AI-21 #302) or BILLING (#79). The highest valid inbox plan wins (MAX > PRO > PLUS > FREE, period_start <= now < valid_until); equal plans use the latest received_at, then the later period_start, then descending snapshot_id. Without a valid inbox snapshot the configured plan applies. Only a BILLING snapshot spanning more than two months reports period YEAR; PROMO always reports MONTH, regardless of gift duration. Both grant the plan's monthly allowance each calendar month, never twelve allowances at once. validUntil is the snapshot expiry. Only EntitlementInbox.accept writes it; a browser parameter or return URL never changes it (AI-19, #301).
usageResponseFields.credits.total: Bar size for the period. unlocked is how much of it may be spent now: all of it on paid plans; on FREE the sum of the portions unlocked so far (13 on the 1st, then on each following Monday).
usageResponseFields.dailyBurst: Paid plans only: limits the DEBITS of one calendar day to 35% of the bar. null on FREE. deferredUntil is set while steps wait for the next day.
usageResponseFields.weeklyUnlock: FREE only: portions [13, 13, 12, 12], how many are unlocked, the next unlock instant (Monday 00:00 Europe/Moscow) and its size. null on paid plans.
usageResponseFields.fairUse: Quiet counters outside the bar (speech-to-text, answer checks).
usageResponseFields.caps: Count caps per window; limit 0 means not offered on the plan.

estimateRequest.description: Exactly one of spec (a generation spec, see generation/http.json schemas.generationSpec) or edit.

estimateResponseFields.credits: p95 is the sum of rate card weights and is what a reservation holds; p50 is the same formula with typical weights = weight x 0.6 until measured weights exist (rate-card-v1.json estimation).
estimateResponseFields.percentOfPeriodAllowance: The composer shows 'about N% of the monthly limit' from p95, over the period bar.
estimateResponseFields.budget: Set when spec.settings.budgetPercent is given: {percent, capCredits}; capCredits = percent x remaining at estimate time, becomes the reservation cap and the planner input.
estimateResponseFields.canStart: false when any bucket blocks. The button stays enabled; pressing it explains the options (409 USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED).
estimateResponseFields.blockingBuckets: Present when canStart is false: one entry per blocking bucket with the members of the USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED problem (bucket, window, unit, limit, used, required, offered, renewsAt, fitsAfterRenewal, plan).
estimateResponseFields.warnings[].code: PERSONAL_DATA_SUSPECTED: a fragment of a source looks like personal data; ranges are UTF-16 offsets into the source text; the response never echoes the fragment. Mandatory server-side redaction of email, phone and card-number patterns happens regardless; this warning is the optional user-facing exclusion.

reservation.description: usage_reservation. A hold on the balance, scoped to one admission. SESSION reservations cover the INITIAL batch only; every later chargeable action creates its own small reservation.

scopes.SESSION: Created with the session in one transaction (hold = estimate p95 of the initial batch, or the budget cap). When the session enters REVIEW (no QUEUED or GENERATING artifact) the unspent remainder is RELEASED.
scopes.TURN: One edit turn (EDIT_SELECTION, IMAGE_SEARCH, IMAGE_GENERATE, AUDIO_REGENERATE) or one media redo; created at admission, bound to the turn.
scopes.STEP: One retryArtifact (the regenerated artifact's steps) or one deferred step that must re-reserve after a period rollover.

states.SETTLED: Ended with at least one debit; the unspent remainder was returned. Applies when the session reaches REVIEW, or is CLOSED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED or deleted after a debit.
states.RELEASED: Ended without any debit; the whole hold was returned (session reached REVIEW with nothing spent, cancelled, deleted or expired).
states.EXPIRED: An orphaned hold passed its expiresAt and was returned.

transitions.trigger: admission (session created, edit accepted, retry accepted)
transitions.guard: the conditional update on usage_balance succeeds, else 409 USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED before any state change

transitions.trigger: scope finished (session in REVIEW, turn applied or failed, step finished) after at least one DEBIT; also session CLOSED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED or deleted after a DEBIT
scope finished or cancelled with no DEBIT; the session entered REVIEW with nothing spent; deleted or expired with nothing spent

reservation.periodRule: A reservation carries periodId. Its debits draw from that period's balance. A reservation never outlives its period: expiresAt = min(learning.usage.reservation-ttl, period end). At period rollover every ACTIVE hold is released and the remaining steps re-reserve in the new period.
reservation.neverNegative: Admission is ONE conditional update on usage_balance inside the admission transaction: UPDATE usage_balance SET reserved = reserved + :hold, row_version = row_version + 1 WHERE available >= :hold AND row_version = :v. Zero rows updated means 409 USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED. Two concurrent admissions cannot both pass because both compete for the same row version and the loser re-reads a smaller available. `available` is unlocked - used - reserved.
invariants: debitedCredits never exceeds heldCredits; a call whose cost would exceed the remaining hold is not made (artifact FAILED with ESTIMATE_EXCEEDED; a retry re-reserves). A user's limit that cannot cover the call fails with USAGE_LIMIT.
A user never goes negative: credits.remaining >= 0.
A FAILED step caused by the provider is not debited; a repair inside a successful step is.

The daily burst limits DEBITS per calendar day, not reservations: admission checks the monthly availability only, a running step whose debit would exceed the burst completes, further steps that day wait in READY with next_attempt_at at the next day start and USAGE_UPDATED carries deferredUntil.

ledger.description: usage_ledger_entry: append-only; usage_balance is materialized in the same transaction. idempotencyKey is UNIQUE, so a retried write is a no-op. A DEBIT draws from the period of its reservation.

GRANT.meaning: Allowance for a period or a Free weekly portion; produced from an entitlement snapshot.

DEBIT.meaning: Consumption by a step result, in the transaction that stores the result.

REFUND.meaning: Return of a debit (for example a provider-side failure found later).

ADJUSTMENT.meaning: Operator correction with an audit reference.

EXPIRE.meaning: Unspent allowance removed at the end of its period; there is no rollover to the next month.

ledger.ledgerNotes: costMicros is the measured provider cost in millionths of a rouble; credits is what the rate card charged. The gap is the input for the 14-day weight review.

errors.note: renewsAt is null when waiting will not help (offered=false). fitsAfterRenewal is true when the required amount fits the bucket after the next refresh or unlock only. STT and ASSESSMENT limits are fair-use: exceeding them returns the same code from their own endpoints (AI-15, AI-20); they are not debited from the bar.
